name: Bolivia

findings.controller: China National Electronics Import & Export Corporation (CEIEC)
findings.summary: BOL-110 citizen-security command-and-control system, built by Chinese state firm CEIEC on two China Eximbank concessional loans, went live in La Paz and El Alto with facial-recognition cameras, drones and patrol links; phase two covered six further cities.
findings.analyst_inference: AidData (research database, treated S2) names CEIEC as contractor and China Eximbank as lender (two RMB 350m loans, 2016 and 2018) and records both phases complete on 2019-08-20; eju.tv/La Razon confirm 'a Chinese firm' built it. Announced total ~US$105m (US$50m phase 1 + US$55m phase 2) per Bolivian press. Coded prc on the equipment/integrator rule; camera brand not identified. Pre-2020 and still_current unconfirmed: no source checked whether CEIEC still maintains the system or whether the Paz government (from Nov 2025) has reviewed it.

findings.summary: China donated 570 video-surveillance cameras to Bolivia's national police for monitoring centres in La Paz, El Alto, Cochabamba and Santa Cruz; brand and value were not reported.

sources.publisher: eju.tv (credited to ABI, Bolivian state news agency)

findings.analyst_inference: Sole source is Bolivian state news agency ABI via eju.tv, so S4. Tier 4 (equipment delivered) as operational scale is not shown. Camera vendor unknown; likely PRC-made but not stated. Pre-2020; still_current not checked.

findings.controller: China Academy of Space Technology / China Great Wall Industry Corporation
findings.builder: China Great Wall Industry Corporation (prime contractor, per ASP)
findings.summary: Bolivia's Tupac Katari (TKSat-1) communications satellite, built by CAST on the DFH-4 bus and launched from Xichang in December 2013 with China Development Bank loan support, is operated by state agency ABE from two Bolivian ground stations.
findings.analyst_inference: Coded networks/prc on the equipment-vendor rule (Chinese builder supplies satellite firmware); ABE is the operator. NASASpaceFlight names CAST and CDB; DPL News (2024) confirms China launch, ABE operation and ~US$302m investment, revenue still flowing in 2024. ASP (think tank, S4) says CGWIC was prime contractor, CDB lent ~85% over 16 years, ground stations were CGWIC-built and the satellite retires ~2028; it also relays expert claims of persistent Beijing access, unverified. Value figures conflict (US$290m vs US$302m) so not coded. still_current null: operation in 2026 not confirmed in this pass.

findings.summary: State operator Entel and Huawei ran Bolivia's first 5G tests at the Expocruz fair in Santa Cruz in September 2019, reaching about 1.1 Gbit/s.
findings.analyst_inference: Tier 2 (pilot/demonstration). No source opened in this pass names the vendor of Entel's 2025 commercial 5G rollout (100+ sites in nine capitals, US$47.5m projected by Dec 2025 per DPL News), nor its 4G RAN/core vendor; Huawei is plausible incumbent but unconfirmed. A 2019 DPL News report relays a businessman's allegation that Entel's 2014 LTE router tender was steered to Huawei (no investigation reported); not coded.

findings.summary: Millicom picked Ericsson to modernise Tigo's mobile networks in three Latin American markets including Bolivia, covering Ericsson Radio System equipment, replacement of the 4G core and a 5G dual-mode core.
findings.analyst_inference: Ericsson is Swedish, so third pole. The article gives no Bolivia-specific breakdown, so the scope in Bolivia is inferred from the three-country programme. Value undisclosed. Viva (NuevaTel) vendor not found.

findings.summary: State telco Entel opened a roughly 4,500 sqm, US$52 million data centre in El Alto, which President Arce said would host public and private data; the builder and equipment vendors were not reported.
findings.analyst_inference: Owner-operator Entel is Bolivian state-owned, so domestic. Tier 5 on the reported launch; not an AI-specific facility. IT equipment vendor (possibly Huawei, given Entel's history) unknown.

findings.controller: Amazon / Oracle / Tesla (named by President Paz)
findings.summary: President Rodrigo Paz said Tesla, Amazon, Oracle and other foreign firms would from January 2026 invest in the first government-promoted data centres in El Alto and Cochabamba; no agreement, value or operator was reported.
findings.analyst_inference: Tier 1 statement of intent only; coded us because all named firms are US, but no controller is confirmed. No follow-up announcement found in this pass. Read as part of the Paz government's US-facing pivot (analyst inference).

findings.local_actor: Ministerio de Obras Publicas, Servicios y Vivienda
findings.summary: Supreme Decree 5509, promulgated under President Paz, authorised Starlink, OneWeb and Amazon's Kuiper to operate satellite internet in Bolivia.
findings.analyst_inference: Coded tier 4 as an operating authorisation (licence-equivalent); actual service launch not confirmed. Mixed pole: Starlink and Kuiper are US, OneWeb third (UK/France); coded us as dominant. Analyst inference: opening to US LEO providers sits alongside the PRC-built Tupac Katari (BOL-003) but is not a reversal of it.

silicon.null_reason: no accelerator purchases or deployments surfaced in data-centre and AI searches; no dedicated silicon search

models.null_reason: no national model or government frontier-model partnership found; AGETIC June 2026 bulletin mentions 'ethical AI sovereignty' and a C.E.R.E.B.R.O. platform with no named provider
